title: AI-Enhanced Biosensing from CT Imaging: A CIOF-Based Deep Learning Framework for Pulmonary Embolism Detection
content: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a critical cardiovascular condition requiring rapid and accurate detection. This study presents an AI-enhanced biosensing framework utilizing computed tomography angiography (CTA) as an imaging-based sensor platform for automated PE diagnosis. Deep learning-based semantic segmentation models were employed to extract pathophysiological signals indicative of emboli. We utilized the publicly available FUMPE dataset, containing 2,304 annotated CTA slices from 35 patients. Ten fully convolutional networks (FCNs) were trained using five backbone architectures each optimized with both Adam and SGDM algorithms. To improve robustness and mitigate model-specific biases, we propose a novel Consensus Intersection-Optimized Fusion (CIOF) method, which adaptively aggregates multi-model predictions to maximize overlap with ground truth. CIOF achieved only 41 missed detections, outperforming all individual models (e.g., InceptionResNetV2+Adam: 411 misses). Performance was evaluated using IoU, Dice coefficient, boundary-based F1 score, and the number of segmented regions. The CIOF mechanism emulates intelligent signal fusion in biosensing applications and supports real-time integration with diagnostic imaging platforms. This work highlights CIOF as a promising AI-driven ensemble fusion strategy for medical biosensing, offering potential for integration into smart diagnostic systems, computer-aided tools, and future wearable biosensor-assisted triage technologies.
